children: By Isabella Simonetti and Andrew Tangel
Amazon.com is pausing its operations with 21 Air, the cargo carrier that was operating the Amazon-branded plane that crashed in Miami, killing five people.
Amazon said it notified 21 Air leadership of the decision on Sunday.

"Safety has always been our top priority, whether in our own operations or when we're working with partners," Amazon spokeswoman Kelly Nantel said. "We'll continue working to support the investigation and everyone affected."
A spokesman for 21 Air didn't immediately comment late Sunday.
An Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway at Miami International Airport a week ago, crashing into nearby vehicles and skidding to a stop 1,300 feet past the runway with its right engine on fire.

The National Transportation Safety Board is probing the accident. Investigators released details last week that indicated the two pilots belatedly decided to redo their landing before deciding to brake and stop the plane. 21 Air's safety practices, its arrangement with Amazon and the pilots' actions are among the NTSB's lines of inquiry into the accident.
21 Air is a small cargo carrier owned by Jim Crane, a logistics magnate and owner of the Houston Astros baseball team. The airline flies for carriers such as Amazon and DHL Express.
21 Air operates about 17 planes. Eight of the company's planes fly for Amazon, which has worked with the airline for nearly two years.
Amazon deferred questions on the investigation to the NTSB.
